library(DHARMa)      # residual diagnostics

# Overview

Habitat stratum is fitted as a **fixed effect** throughout the main analysis.
This appendix documents the evidence behind that specification. It was
originally prepared as a comparison between a random intercept and a fixed
effect; the comparison came down decisively on the side of the fixed effect, and
the main analysis was refitted accordingly. What follows is the record of that
comparison.

Two properties of the design make the fixed effect the appropriate estimator on
first principles. With only five strata (open, forest, harvest, linear,
riparian), a variance component is estimated from four degrees of freedom, which
is not enough to determine it reliably. More importantly, the five strata are
exhaustive categories fixed by the sampling design rather than a sample drawn
from a wider population of strata, which is the condition for a fixed
effect.

The empirical case is set out below. Each section is stated as a question,
because that is how the comparison was run. The answers are what justify the
specification. In summary: the stratum variance is estimated at or near zero in
most elk models, so the random intercept was not absorbing stratum differences
at all; AIC prefers the fixed effect in 9 of the 10 species-period combinations;
the collinearity cost that would have argued for partial pooling does not
materialise, with no variance inflation factor exceeding 4.03 and no model
failing to converge; and the inference the paper reports is largely preserved,
with the changes concentrated at fine spatial extents where stratum and the
habitat predictors are confounded.

Two scoping decisions:

1. **Predictor sets are held fixed.** The base predictor sets used for the
   profile comparison were selected by the dredge procedure in S7 under the
   random-intercept specification. Comparing profiles under two specifications
   *and* two predictor sets would change two things at once and would make any
   difference impossible to attribute. The sets used in the comparison are
   therefore taken verbatim from the original S7 run and applied to both
   specifications. The final section then re-runs selection itself under both
   specifications, and reports where the selected sets differ.
2. **Only base models are refit.** Substitution and univariate models inherit
   the same stratum term, so the base models are a sufficient test of whether the
   specification matters.

All functions in Section 3 are duplicated from S7, with the single exception of
the stratum term in `fit_nb_glmm()`, which is switchable here and documented
inline. 

# Data Preparation

The preparation below reproduces S7 exactly: drop locations where the human-use
predictor is NA, impute structural NDVI NAs to zero, compute the spatial
autocovariate, and build the pooled cattle and elk datasets.

```{r load-and-prepare}
dat_raw <- read_csv(data_file, show_col_types = FALSE)

# Spatial scales (16 radii)
all_scales <- sort(unique(dat_raw$extent_radius_m))

habitat_covars <- c("p_herb", "NDVI_herb", "p_shrub", "p_harvest",
                    "p_wetland", "hu", "tri")

# Temporal structures (identical to S7)
horse_months <- 5:10
cattle_bimonthly <- list("Jul-Aug" = c(7, 8), "Sep-Oct" = c(9, 10))
elk_quarterly    <- list("May-Jul" = c(5, 6, 7), "Aug-Oct" = c(8, 9, 10))

# Drop rows with NA hu (edge locations outside the IDW interpolation extent),
# then impute NDVI_herb NA to 0 (occurs where p_herb = 0).
dat <- dat_raw %>%
  filter(!is.na(hu)) %>%
  mutate(
    NDVI_herb = replace_na(NDVI_herb, 0),
    # Explicit factor so that both the (1|strata) and the fixed-effect
    # specifications see the same level ordering. Open is the reference level:
    # it is one of the information-rich strata, whereas Forest has as few as 4
    # non-zero detection rows in some species-periods and would inflate every
    # contrast estimated against it. Matches the declaration used in S6 and S7.
    strata    = factor(strata, levels = c("Open", "Forest", "Harvest", "Linear", "Riparian"))
  )

cat("Rows after preparation:", nrow(dat), "\n")
cat("Strata levels (reference first):", paste(levels(dat$strata), collapse = ", "), "\n")
```

```{r compute-sac}
# ── Duplicated verbatim from S7 ──
compute_sac <- function(data, bandwidth_km = 20) {
  n <- nrow(data)
  if (n < 2) return(rep(NA_real_, n))

  coords   <- as.matrix(data[, c("longitude", "latitude")])
  det_rate <- data$n_det / data$camera_days

  # Approximate km conversion for the Alberta foothills (~51 N)
  lat_km    <- coords[, 2] * 111.32
  lon_km    <- coords[, 1] * 111.32 * cos(mean(coords[, 2]) * pi / 180)
  coords_km <- cbind(lon_km, lat_km)
  dist_km   <- as.matrix(dist(coords_km))

  sac_values <- numeric(n)
  for (i in seq_len(n)) {
    neighbours <- which(dist_km[i, ] > 0 & dist_km[i, ] <= bandwidth_km)
    if (length(neighbours) == 0) {
      sac_values[i] <- NA_real_
    } else {
      weights <- 1 / dist_km[i, neighbours]
      sac_values[i] <- sum(weights * det_rate[neighbours]) / sum(weights)
    }
  }
  sac_values
}

ref_scale <- all_scales[1]

sac_df <- dat %>%
  filter(extent_radius_m == ref_scale) %>%
  group_by(species, year, month) %>%
  mutate(sac = compute_sac(pick(everything()), bandwidth_km = 20)) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  dplyr::select(location, species, year, month, sac)

dat <- dat %>%
  left_join(sac_df, by = c("location", "species", "year", "month"))

cat("SAC NAs:", sum(is.na(dat$sac)), "\n")
```

```{r pooled-datasets}
# ── Duplicated verbatim from S7 ──
pool_months <- function(data, month_vec, period_label) {
  data %>%
    filter(month %in% month_vec) %>%
    group_by(location, species, year, extent_radius_m, strata, strata_code,
             latitude, longitude) %>%
    summarise(
      n_det       = sum(n_det),
      camera_days = sum(camera_days),
      p_herb    = first(p_herb),
      p_shrub   = first(p_shrub),
      p_wetland = first(p_wetland),
      p_harvest = first(p_harvest),
      tri       = first(tri),
      NDVI_herb = mean(NDVI_herb, na.rm = TRUE),
      hu        = mean(hu,        na.rm = TRUE),
      sac       = mean(sac,       na.rm = TRUE),
      .groups = "drop"
    ) %>%
    mutate(
      log_effort = log(camera_days),
      period     = period_label
    ) %>%
    filter(camera_days >= 7)
}

cattle_bimonthly_data <- map2_dfr(
  cattle_bimonthly, names(cattle_bimonthly),
  ~ pool_months(filter(dat, species == "Cattle"), .x, .y)
)

elk_quarterly_data <- map2_dfr(
  elk_quarterly, names(elk_quarterly),
  ~ pool_months(filter(dat, species == "Elk"), .x, .y)
)

horse_data <- dat %>% filter(species == "Horse")
```

# Model Fitting Functions

```{r model-functions}
# ── Duplicated from S7, with ONE modification ──
# `strata_effect` selects the stratum term. The default, "random", reproduces
# S7's behaviour exactly; "fixed" replaces (1|strata) with strata as a set of
# fixed effects. Nothing else in this function differs from S7.
fit_nb_glmm <- function(data, covars, scale_m, standardize = TRUE,
                        strata_effect = c("random", "fixed")) {

  strata_effect <- match.arg(strata_effect)

  d <- data %>% filter(extent_radius_m == scale_m)
  if (nrow(d) < 10) return(NULL)

  # Standardize predictors (including the SAC), as in S7
  vars_to_scale <- c(covars, "sac")
  for (v in vars_to_scale) {
    if (v %in% names(d)) d[[v]] <- as.numeric(scale(d[[v]]))
  }

  fixed_terms <- paste(c(covars, "sac"), collapse = " + ")

  # ── THE ONLY DIFFERENCE BETWEEN THE TWO SPECIFICATIONS ──
  strata_term <- if (strata_effect == "random") "(1|strata)" else "strata"

  form <- as.formula(
    paste0("n_det ~ ", fixed_terms, " + ", strata_term, " + offset(log_effort)")
  )

  tryCatch({
    mod <- glmmTMB(form, data = d, family = nbinom2)
    if (!mod$sdr$pdHess) {
      warning("Non-positive-definite Hessian at scale ", scale_m)
    }
    mod
  }, error = function(e) {
    warning("Model failed at scale ", scale_m, ": ", e$message)
    NULL
  })
}


# ── Duplicated from S7, with conf.low / conf.high added to the failure stub ──
# so that failed fits bind cleanly with successful ones.
tidy_model <- function(mod, species, period, scale_m, model_type, covars_in_model) {

  null_row <- tibble(
    species = species, period = period, extent_radius_m = scale_m,
    model_type = model_type,
    covars_in_model = paste(covars_in_model, collapse = "+"),
    term = NA_character_, estimate = NA_real_, std.error = NA_real_,
    statistic = NA_real_, p.value = NA_real_,
    conf.low = NA_real_, conf.high = NA_real_,
    converged = FALSE, AIC = NA_real_
  )

  if (is.null(mod)) return(null_row)

  tryCatch({
    broom.mixed::tidy(mod, effects = "fixed", conf.int = TRUE) %>%
      mutate(
        species         = species,
        period          = period,
        extent_radius_m = scale_m,
        model_type      = model_type,
        covars_in_model = paste(covars_in_model, collapse = "+"),
        converged       = mod$sdr$pdHess,
        AIC             = AIC(mod)
      )
  }, error = function(e) null_row)
}


# Extract the stratum random-effect SD from a fitted glmmTMB model.
# Returns NA for the fixed-effect specification, where no such term exists.
extract_strata_sd <- function(mod) {
  if (is.null(mod)) return(NA_real_)
  tryCatch(sqrt(VarCorr(mod)$cond$strata[1, 1]), error = function(e) NA_real_)
}
```

# Model Configuration

```{r configuration}
# Base predictor sets selected under the random-intercept specification in the
# original S7 run, held fixed for this comparison (see the scoping decisions above).
# Manuscript Table 2 gives the selection under the fixed-effect specification, which
# differs for cattle; the final section of this document re-runs the selection.
base_covars <- list(
  Horse  = c("tri", "hu", "p_harvest", "p_wetland", "p_shrub"),
  Cattle = c("hu", "tri", "p_herb", "p_wetland"),
  Elk    = c("hu", "p_harvest")
)

# Return the analysis dataset for one species x period combination
get_period_data <- function(sp, per) {
  if (sp == "Horse") {
    horse_data %>% filter(month == match(per, month.abb))
  } else if (sp == "Cattle") {
    cattle_bimonthly_data %>% filter(period == per)
  } else {
    elk_quarterly_data %>% filter(period == per)
  }
}

# The 10 species x period combinations used in the main analysis
jobs <- bind_rows(
  tibble(species = "Horse",  period = month.abb[horse_months]),
  tibble(species = "Cattle", period = names(cattle_bimonthly)),
  tibble(species = "Elk",    period = names(elk_quarterly))
)

# Full fitting grid: 10 combinations x 16 extents x 2 specifications
fit_grid <- expand_grid(
  jobs,
  extent_radius_m = all_scales,
  spec            = c("random", "fixed")
)

cat("Model fits to run:", nrow(fit_grid), "\n")
```

# Fit Both Specifications

```{r fit-both}
results_raw <- future_pmap_dfr(
  fit_grid,
  function(species, period, extent_radius_m, spec) {
    d      <- get_period_data(species, period)
    covars <- base_covars[[species]]

    mod <- fit_nb_glmm(d, covars, extent_radius_m, strata_effect = spec)

    # Evaluate BOTH of these before the mutate(). Inside mutate(), once `spec`
    # has been assigned as a column, any later reference to `spec` resolves to
    # that column (length n) rather than to this function argument (length 1),
    # which makes if() fail with "the condition has length > 1".
    spec_val <- spec
    sd_val   <- if (identical(spec, "random")) extract_strata_sd(mod) else NA_real_

    tidy_model(mod, species, period, extent_radius_m, "base", covars) %>%
      mutate(spec = spec_val, strata_sd = sd_val)
  },
  .options  = furrr_options(seed = TRUE),
  .progress = TRUE
)

# Keep only the habitat predictors. This drops the intercept, the SAC, the
# dispersion component, and (under the fixed specification) the four stratum
# level coefficients, which are nuisance terms here.
results <- results_raw %>%
  filter(term %in% unlist(base_covars)) %>%
  mutate(
    spec    = factor(spec, levels = c("random", "fixed"),
                     labels = c("Random intercept", "Fixed effect")),
    species = factor(species, levels = c("Horse", "Cattle", "Elk"))
  )

cat("Converged fits:",
    results_raw %>% distinct(species, period, extent_radius_m, spec, converged) %>%
      pull(converged) %>% sum(na.rm = TRUE),
    "of", nrow(fit_grid), "\n")
```

# Is the Random Effect Well Estimated?

The first question is whether the random intercept was estimating anything. If
the stratum variance is estimated near zero, partial pooling has gone to
completion, all five stratum baselines have been shrunk onto a single number,
and the fitted model is equivalent to one carrying no stratum term at all. That
is a failure of estimation rather than a finding, and glmmTMB issues no warning
when it happens.

```{r variance-components}
varcomp <- results_raw %>%
  filter(spec == "random") %>%
  distinct(species, period, extent_radius_m, strata_sd) %>%
  group_by(species, period) %>%
  summarise(
    n_models   = n(),
    sd_min     = min(strata_sd,    na.rm = TRUE),
    sd_median  = median(strata_sd, na.rm = TRUE),
    sd_max     = max(strata_sd,    na.rm = TRUE),
    # A near-zero SD indicates a boundary (effectively singular) fit
    n_near_zero = sum(strata_sd < 1e-4, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

kable(varcomp, digits = 3,
      caption = "**Table S8.1.** Stratum random-effect standard deviation (log scale) across the 16 spatial extents, by species and period. Near-zero values indicate boundary fits where the random effect is effectively absent.") %>%
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover"), full_width = FALSE)
```

# Do the Reported Results Change?

The paper reports two things per profile: the **peak scale of effect** and the
**domain structure** (the number and sign of contiguous runs where the 95% CI
excludes zero). The function below extracts both, using the same definitions as
the main text.

```{r profile-summaries}
# Summarise one species x period x predictor x specification profile
# across the 16 spatial extents.
profile_summary <- function(d) {
  d <- arrange(d, extent_radius_m)

  # A cell is "non-zero" when the 95% CI excludes zero
  sig <- !is.na(d$conf.low) & !is.na(d$conf.high) &
         (d$conf.low > 0 | d$conf.high < 0)
  sgn <- ifelse(sig, sign(d$estimate), 0)

  # Contiguous runs of identical non-zero sign = domains of scale
  r      <- rle(sgn)
  n_dom  <- sum(r$values != 0)
  signs  <- paste(ifelse(r$values[r$values != 0] > 0, "+", "-"), collapse = "")

  if (any(sig)) {
    i         <- which(sig)[which.max(abs(d$estimate[sig]))]
    peak      <- d$extent_radius_m[i]
    peak_est  <- d$estimate[i]
  } else {
    peak <- NA_real_; peak_est <- NA_real_
  }

  tibble(
    n_sig_extents = sum(sig),
    n_domains     = n_dom,
    domain_signs  = if (signs == "") NA_character_ else signs,
    peak_extent_m = peak,
    peak_estimate = peak_est
  )
}

profiles <- results %>%
  group_by(species, period, term, spec) %>%
  group_modify(~ profile_summary(.x)) %>%
  ungroup()
```

```{r profile-comparison}
comparison <- profiles %>%
  pivot_wider(
    names_from  = spec,
    values_from = c(n_sig_extents, n_domains, domain_signs,
                    peak_extent_m, peak_estimate),
    names_sep   = "_"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    peak_match   = `peak_extent_m_Random intercept` == `peak_extent_m_Fixed effect`,
    # Treat two profiles with no non-zero domain anywhere as matching
    peak_match   = if_else(is.na(`peak_extent_m_Random intercept`) &
                           is.na(`peak_extent_m_Fixed effect`), TRUE, peak_match),
    domain_match = `domain_signs_Random intercept` == `domain_signs_Fixed effect`,
    domain_match = if_else(is.na(`domain_signs_Random intercept`) &
                           is.na(`domain_signs_Fixed effect`), TRUE, domain_match)
  )

cat("Profiles compared:", nrow(comparison), "\n")
cat("Peak scale identical:  ", sum(comparison$peak_match,   na.rm = TRUE),
    "of", nrow(comparison), "\n")
cat("Domain structure identical:", sum(comparison$domain_match, na.rm = TRUE),
    "of", nrow(comparison), "\n")

kable(
  comparison %>%
    dplyr::select(species, period, term,
                  `peak_extent_m_Random intercept`, `peak_extent_m_Fixed effect`,
                  peak_match,
                  `domain_signs_Random intercept`, `domain_signs_Fixed effect`,
                  domain_match) %>%
    arrange(species, period, term),
  col.names = c("Species", "Period", "Predictor",
                "Peak (random)", "Peak (fixed)", "Peak match",
                "Domains (random)", "Domains (fixed)", "Domain match"),
  caption = "**Table S8.2.** Peak scale of effect (m) and domain structure under each specification. Domain signs read fine to broad scale; NA indicates no non-zero domain at any extent."
) %>%
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover"), full_width = FALSE)
```

## Cell-level agreement

A stricter test than the profile summaries: across every species x period x
predictor x extent cell, does the sign classification (positive non-zero,
negative non-zero, or CI crossing zero) agree between specifications?

```{r cell-agreement}
cells <- results %>%
  mutate(
    class = case_when(
      is.na(conf.low) | is.na(conf.high) ~ NA_character_,
      conf.low  > 0                      ~ "positive",
      conf.high < 0                      ~ "negative",
      TRUE                               ~ "zero"
    )
  ) %>%
  dplyr::select(species, period, term, extent_radius_m, spec, class, estimate) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = spec, values_from = c(class, estimate), names_sep = "_")

agreement <- cells %>%
  summarise(
    n_cells   = n(),
    n_agree   = sum(`class_Random intercept` == `class_Fixed effect`, na.rm = TRUE),
    pct_agree = 100 * n_agree / n_cells,
    # Correlation of the point estimates themselves
    r_estimates = cor(`estimate_Random intercept`, `estimate_Fixed effect`,
                      use = "complete.obs")
  )

kable(agreement, digits = c(0, 0, 1, 3),
      col.names = c("Cells", "Agreeing", "% agreement", "r (estimates)"),
      caption = "**Table S8.3.** Cell-level agreement in sign classification and correlation of point estimates between the two specifications.") %>%
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover"), full_width = FALSE)

# Where do the disagreements sit?
disagreements <- cells %>%
  filter(`class_Random intercept` != `class_Fixed effect`) %>%
  arrange(species, period, term, extent_radius_m)

if (nrow(disagreements) > 0) {
  kable(disagreements, digits = 3,
        caption = "**Table S8.4.** Cells where the sign classification differs between specifications.") %>%
    kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover"), full_width = FALSE)
} else {
  cat("No cell-level disagreements.\n")
}
```

Rows are predictors and columns species and period; lines are standardized coefficients (log-rate scale) across the 16 extents, with shaded 95% confidence intervals."}
ggplot(results, aes(x = extent_radius_m, y = estimate,
                    colour = spec, fill = spec)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey40") +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = conf.low, ymax = conf.high),

  scale_colour_manual(values = c("Random intercept" = "#2C7FB8",

  scale_fill_manual(values   = c("Random intercept" = "#2C7FB8",
                                 "Fixed effect"     = "#D95F02")) +
  labs(
    title    = "Scale-of-effect profiles: stratum as random intercept vs. fixed effect",
    subtitle = "Standardized coefficients (log-rate scale) with 95% confidence intervals",
    x        = "Buffer radius (m, log scale)",
    y        = "Standardized coefficient",
    colour   = "Stratum term", fill = "Stratum term"
  ) +
  theme_bw(base_size = 11) +
  theme(legend.position = "top",
        strip.text = element_text(size = 8))
```

# Collinearity Between Stratum and the Habitat Predictors

The strongest argument that could be made for retaining the random intercept is
that the five strata overlap with the habitat predictors, so entering them as
fixed effects makes the stratum term and the predictors compete for the same
variance. The two diagnostics below are what test it.

The same overlap cuts the other way, and this is the substantive reason the
specification matters rather than a technicality. Where a predictor is strongly
confounded with stratum, any stratum difference the random intercept fails to
absorb does not vanish: it is attributed to whichever predictor most resembles
habitat type. The confounding is concentrated at fine spatial extents, which is
where the two specifications differ most and where the broad-scale results are
unaffected.

Two diagnostics below. First, how much of each predictor's variance the strata
alone explain, which identifies *which* predictors are confounded with stratum.
Second, variance inflation factors for the habitat predictors with and without
strata as fixed effects. Note that the "without strata" design matrix is exactly
the fixed-effect structure of the random-intercept model, so the difference
between the two columns is the collinearity cost of the fixed specification.

VIF is invariant to linear rescaling, so no standardization is needed here.

```{r vif-functions}
# Variance inflation factors computed directly from the fixed-effects design
# matrix. VIF_j = SST_j / SSE_j from regressing column j on all other columns,
# which avoids a dependency on car or performance.
compute_vif <- function(data, covars, scale_m, include_strata = TRUE) {

  d <- data %>% filter(extent_radius_m == scale_m)
  if (nrow(d) < 10) return(NULL)

  rhs <- paste(c(covars, "sac", if (include_strata) "strata"), collapse = " + ")
  X   <- model.matrix(as.formula(paste("~", rhs)), data = d)
  X   <- X[, colnames(X) != "(Intercept)", drop = FALSE]

  # Drop any zero-variance column (e.g. a stratum absent from this subset)
  X <- X[, apply(X, 2, function(z) var(z) > 0), drop = FALSE]
  if (ncol(X) < 2) return(NULL)

  vifs <- vapply(seq_len(ncol(X)), function(j) {
    y   <- X[, j]
    Z   <- cbind(1, X[, -j, drop = FALSE])
    fit <- tryCatch(lm.fit(Z, y), error = function(e) NULL)
    if (is.null(fit)) return(NA_real_)
    sse <- sum(fit$residuals^2)
    sst <- sum((y - mean(y))^2)
    if (sst <= 0) return(NA_real_)
    if (sse <= 0) return(Inf)          # perfect collinearity
    sst / sse
  }, numeric(1))

  tibble(term = colnames(X), vif = vifs)
}


# Proportion of each predictor's variance explained by stratum alone.
# High values identify predictors confounded with the sampling stratification.
covariate_strata_r2 <- function(data, covars, scale_m) {
  d <- data %>% filter(extent_radius_m == scale_m)
  if (nrow(d) < 10) return(NULL)

  map_dfr(c(covars, "sac"), function(v) {
    tibble(
      term         = v,
      r2_on_strata = summary(lm(d[[v]] ~ d$strata))$r.squared
    )
  })
}
```

## How confounded is each predictor with stratum?

```{r covariate-strata-confounding}
confounding <- pmap_dfr(
  expand_grid(jobs, extent_radius_m = all_scales),
  function(species, period, extent_radius_m) {
    d   <- get_period_data(species, period)
    res <- covariate_strata_r2(d, base_covars[[species]], extent_radius_m)
    if (is.null(res)) return(NULL)
    res %>% mutate(species = species, period = period,
                   extent_radius_m = extent_radius_m)
  }
)

confounding_summary <- confounding %>%
  filter(term != "sac") %>%
  group_by(species, term) %>%
  summarise(
    r2_min    = min(r2_on_strata),
    r2_median = median(r2_on_strata),
    r2_max    = max(r2_on_strata),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  arrange(desc(r2_median))

kable(confounding_summary, digits = 3,
      col.names = c("Species", "Predictor", "min R2", "median R2", "max R2"),
      caption = "**Table S8.5.** Proportion of each habitat predictor's variance explained by stratum alone, summarised across the 16 spatial extents. Higher values indicate stronger confounding with the sampling stratification.") %>%
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover"), full_width = FALSE)
```

```{r confounding-by-scale, fig.height=6, fig.cap="**Figure S8.2.** Proportion of each habitat predictor's variance explained by sampling stratum (R²), by spatial extent and species."}
ggplot(confounding %>% filter(term != "sac"),
       aes(x = extent_radius_m, y = r2_on_strata, colour = term)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.7) +
  geom_point(size = 1) +
  scale_x_log10() +
  facet_wrap(~ species, ncol = 3) +
  labs(
    title    = "Confounding between habitat predictors and sampling stratum",
    subtitle = "Proportion of predictor variance explained by stratum, by spatial extent",
    x = "Buffer radius (m, log scale)",
    y = expression(R^2~"of predictor on stratum"),
    colour = "Predictor"
  ) +
  theme_bw(base_size = 11) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

## Does the fixed specification inflate variance?

```{r vif-computation}
vif_results <- pmap_dfr(
  expand_grid(jobs, extent_radius_m = all_scales,
              include_strata = c(FALSE, TRUE)),
  function(species, period, extent_radius_m, include_strata) {
    d   <- get_period_data(species, period)
    res <- compute_vif(d, base_covars[[species]], extent_radius_m, include_strata)
    if (is.null(res)) return(NULL)
    res %>% mutate(species = species, period = period,
                   extent_radius_m = extent_radius_m,
                   spec = if (include_strata) "Fixed effect" else "Random intercept")
  }
)

# Habitat predictors only; the stratum dummies are summarised separately below
vif_covars <- vif_results %>%
  filter(term %in% unlist(base_covars))

vif_summary <- vif_covars %>%
  group_by(species, term, spec) %>%
  summarise(vif_median = median(vif, na.rm = TRUE),
            vif_max    = max(vif, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = spec, values_from = c(vif_median, vif_max),
              names_sep = "_") %>%
  mutate(inflation = `vif_median_Fixed effect` / `vif_median_Random intercept`) %>%
  arrange(desc(inflation))

kable(vif_summary, digits = 2,
      caption = "**Table S8.6.** Variance inflation factors for the habitat predictors under each specification, summarised across the 16 spatial extents. The 'Random intercept' columns are the VIFs among the fixed effects when no stratum term is present. `inflation` is the ratio of median VIFs. Values above 5 are conventionally regarded as problematic.") %>%
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover"), full_width = FALSE)

cat("Max VIF for any habitat predictor, random-intercept design:",
    round(max(vif_covars$vif[vif_covars$spec == "Random intercept"], na.rm = TRUE), 2), "\n")
cat("Max VIF for any habitat predictor, fixed-effect design:    ",
    round(max(vif_covars$vif[vif_covars$spec == "Fixed effect"],     na.rm = TRUE), 2), "\n")

# Stratum dummies under the fixed specification
vif_strata <- vif_results %>%
  filter(spec == "Fixed effect", str_starts(term, "strata")) %>%
  group_by(species) %>%
  summarise(vif_median = median(vif, na.rm = TRUE),
            vif_max    = max(vif, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")

kable(vif_strata, digits = 2,
      col.names = c("Species", "Median VIF", "Max VIF"),
      caption = "**Table S8.7.** Variance inflation factors for the stratum dummy variables under the fixed-effect specification.") %>%
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover"), full_width = FALSE)
```

## Standard errors of the affected predictors

If fixed strata genuinely damage estimation, it should show up as wider
confidence intervals, not only as higher VIFs.

```{r se-comparison}
se_comparison <- results %>%
  group_by(species, term, spec) %>%
  summarise(se_median = median(std.error, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = spec, values_from = se_median) %>%
  mutate(se_ratio = `Fixed effect` / `Random intercept`) %>%
  arrange(desc(se_ratio))

kable(se_comparison, digits = 3,
      col.names = c("Species", "Predictor", "Median SE (random)",
                    "Median SE (fixed)", "Ratio"),
      caption = "**Table S8.8.** Median standard errors of the habitat predictors under each specification. A ratio above 1 means the fixed specification estimates that predictor less precisely.") %>%
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover"), full_width = FALSE)
```

# Residual Diagnostics

DHARMa scaled residuals under both specifications, at a single mid-range extent
per species x period to keep runtime manageable. Widen `dharma_scales` to check
more extents.

```{r dharma}
dharma_scales <- all_scales[round(length(all_scales) / 2)]

dharma_results <- expand_grid(jobs, extent_radius_m = dharma_scales,
                              spec = c("random", "fixed")) %>%
  pmap_dfr(function(species, period, extent_radius_m, spec) {
    d      <- get_period_data(species, period)
    covars <- base_covars[[species]]
    mod    <- fit_nb_glmm(d, covars, extent_radius_m, strata_effect = spec)
    if (is.null(mod)) {
      return(tibble(species = species, period = period, spec = spec,
                    ks_p = NA_real_, dispersion_p = NA_real_, outlier_p = NA_real_))
    }
    sim <- simulateResiduals(mod, n = 250, plot = FALSE)
    tibble(
      species = species, period = period, spec = spec,
      ks_p         = testUniformity(sim,  plot = FALSE)$p.value,
      dispersion_p = testDispersion(sim,  plot = FALSE)$p.value,
      outlier_p    = testOutliers(sim,    plot = FALSE)$p.value
    )
  })

kable(dharma_results, digits = 3,
      caption = paste0("**Table S8.9.** DHARMa diagnostic p-values at the ",
                       dharma_scales, " m extent under both specifications. ",
                       "Values below 0.05 indicate residual structure.")) %>%
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover"), full_width = FALSE)
```

# Model Comparison by AIC

Both specifications are fitted by maximum likelihood to identical data, so their
AIC values are comparable. Note that the effective degrees of freedom of a
random intercept are not integer-valued, so the comparison is indicative rather
than decisive.

```{r aic-comparison}
aic_tab <- results_raw %>%
  distinct(species, period, extent_radius_m, spec, AIC) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = spec, values_from = AIC) %>%
  mutate(delta_AIC = fixed - random) %>%
  group_by(species, period) %>%
  summarise(
    n_extents        = n(),
    median_delta_AIC = median(delta_AIC, na.rm = TRUE),
    n_random_better  = sum(delta_AIC > 2,  na.rm = TRUE),
    n_fixed_better   = sum(delta_AIC < -2, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

kable(aic_tab, digits = 2,
      col.names = c("Species", "Period", "Extents", "Median dAIC (fixed - random)",
                    "Random better (dAIC > 2)", "Fixed better (dAIC < -2)"),
      caption = "**Table S8.10.** AIC comparison across spatial extents. Positive median dAIC favours the random-intercept specification.") %>%
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover"), full_width = FALSE)
```

# Would Predictor Selection Change?

The base predictor sets used in the profile comparison above were selected by the
dredge procedure under the random-intercept specification. Selecting under one
model structure and inferring under another is inconsistent, so selection has to
be re-run under the specification the analysis actually uses.

This section re-runs the full dredge under both specifications and compares the
resulting variable-importance rankings. The rankings under the fixed
specification are the ones S7 now uses; the random-intercept column is retained
so the difference is visible.

**Runtime warning.** This is the expensive chunk: 6 combinations x 6 months for
horses, 15 x 2 for cattle and 15 x 2 for elk, each across 16 extents and two
specifications, is 3,072 model fits. Set `run_both_specs <- FALSE` to fit only
the fixed specification and compare against the S7 rankings by hand.

```{r dredge-comparison}
run_both_specs <- TRUE

dredge_covars <- c("p_herb", "p_shrub", "p_harvest", "p_wetland", "hu", "tri")
covar_budget  <- list(Horse = 5, Cattle = 4, Elk = 2)

# ── Duplicated from S7, with strata_effect threaded through ──
dredge_at_scale <- function(data, k, scale_m, covars_to_dredge,
                            strata_effect = "random") {
  combos <- combn(covars_to_dredge, k, simplify = FALSE)

  map_dfr(combos, function(covars) {
    mod <- fit_nb_glmm(data, covars, scale_m, strata_effect = strata_effect)
    tibble(
      covars          = paste(sort(covars), collapse = "+"),
      AIC             = if (is.null(mod)) NA_real_ else AIC(mod),
      extent_radius_m = scale_m
    )
  }) %>%
    filter(!is.na(AIC)) %>%
    mutate(
      delta_AIC  = AIC - min(AIC),
      aic_weight = exp(-0.5 * delta_AIC) / sum(exp(-0.5 * delta_AIC))
    )
}

# ── Duplicated verbatim from S7 ──
compute_variable_importance <- function(dredge_results, covars_to_dredge) {
  map_dfr(covars_to_dredge, function(cv) {
    containing <- dredge_results %>%
      filter(map_lgl(covars, ~ cv %in% str_split(.x, "\\+")[[1]]))
    tibble(
      covariate             = cv,
      cumulative_aic_weight = sum(containing$aic_weight, na.rm = TRUE),
      n_top_model           = sum(containing$delta_AIC == 0, na.rm = TRUE),
      n_models              = nrow(containing)
    )
  }) %>%
    arrange(desc(cumulative_aic_weight))
}

specs_to_run <- if (run_both_specs) c("random", "fixed") else "fixed"

dredge_grid <- expand_grid(jobs, extent_radius_m = all_scales,
                           spec = specs_to_run)

cat("Dredge cells:", nrow(dredge_grid), "\n")
cat("Approximate model fits:",
    sum(choose(length(dredge_covars),
               unlist(covar_budget[as.character(dredge_grid$species)]))), "\n")

dredge_all <- future_pmap_dfr(
  dredge_grid,
  function(species, period, extent_radius_m, spec) {
    d <- get_period_data(species, period)
    dredge_at_scale(d, covar_budget[[species]], extent_radius_m,
                    dredge_covars, strata_effect = spec) %>%
      mutate(species = species, period = period, spec = spec)
  },
  .options  = furrr_options(seed = TRUE),
  .progress = TRUE
)
```

```{r selection-comparison}
importance_by_spec <- dredge_all %>%
  group_by(species, spec) %>%
  group_modify(~ compute_variable_importance(.x, dredge_covars)) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  group_by(species, spec) %>%
  mutate(rank = rank(-cumulative_aic_weight, ties.method = "first")) %>%
  ungroup()

# Side-by-side ranking table
ranking_table <- importance_by_spec %>%
  dplyr::select(species, spec, covariate, cumulative_aic_weight, rank) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = spec,
              values_from = c(cumulative_aic_weight, rank),
              names_sep = "_") %>%
  arrange(species)

kable(ranking_table, digits = 3,
      # Display label only. The underlying column stays `covariate`, which is
      # what importance_by_spec and the dredge output are keyed on.
      col.names = sub("^covariate$", "Predictor", names(ranking_table)),
      caption = "**Table S8.11.** Cumulative AIC weight and rank for each dredge-eligible predictor under both specifications. Ranks above each species' budget form the base model set.") %>%
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover"), full_width = FALSE)

# The decision: does the selected base set change?
selected_sets <- importance_by_spec %>%
  group_by(species, spec) %>%
  filter(rank <= covar_budget[[first(species)]]) %>%
  summarise(base_set = paste(sort(covariate), collapse = ", "), .groups = "drop") %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = spec, values_from = base_set)

if (run_both_specs) {
  selected_sets <- selected_sets %>%
    mutate(unchanged = random == fixed)
}

kable(selected_sets,
      caption = "**Table S8.12.** Selected base predictor set under each specification. `unchanged = TRUE` means adopting fixed stratum effects requires no change to predictor selection.") %>%
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover"), full_width = FALSE)

if (run_both_specs) {
  cat("\nBase set unchanged for",
      sum(selected_sets$unchanged, na.rm = TRUE), "of",
      nrow(selected_sets), "species.\n")
  # Sanity check against the sets used earlier in this document
  cat("\nSets used in the profile comparison above:\n")
  for (sp in names(base_covars)) {
    cat("  ", sp, ":", paste(sort(base_covars[[sp]]), collapse = ", "), "\n")
  }
}
```

# Conclusion

```{r conclusion-numbers, include=FALSE}
# Scalars quoted in the prose below, computed from the objects above so the
# text cannot drift from the tables. No models are fitted here.
n_singular      <- sum(varcomp$n_near_zero, na.rm = TRUE)
n_varcomp_total <- sum(varcomp$n_models,    na.rm = TRUE)
n_singular_elk  <- sum(varcomp$n_near_zero[varcomp$species == "Elk"], na.rm = TRUE)
n_elk_total     <- sum(varcomp$n_models[varcomp$species == "Elk"],    na.rm = TRUE)

n_fixed_favoured <- sum(aic_tab$median_delta_AIC < 0, na.rm = TRUE)
n_periods_total  <- nrow(aic_tab)

n_converged <- results_raw %>%
  distinct(species, period, extent_radius_m, spec, converged) %>%
  pull(converged) %>% sum(na.rm = TRUE)
n_fits <- nrow(fit_grid)

vif_max_fixed  <- max(vif_covars$vif[vif_covars$spec == "Fixed effect"],     na.rm = TRUE)
vif_max_random <- max(vif_covars$vif[vif_covars$spec == "Random intercept"], na.rm = TRUE)

n_se_parity    <- sum(abs(se_comparison$se_ratio - 1) < 0.05, na.rm = TRUE)
n_se_better    <- sum(se_comparison$se_ratio < 1, na.rm = TRUE)
n_se_total     <- nrow(se_comparison)

n_peak_match   <- sum(comparison$peak_match,   na.rm = TRUE)
n_domain_match <- sum(comparison$domain_match, na.rm = TRUE)
n_profiles     <- nrow(comparison)
```

Habitat stratum is fitted as a fixed effect in the main analysis. The evidence
above supports that specification on four counts.

**The random intercept was not estimating what it was asked to estimate.** The
stratum standard deviation came back at or below 1e-4 in `r n_singular` of
`r n_varcomp_total` fits, including `r n_singular_elk` of `r n_elk_total` elk
fits (Table S8.1). At those values partial pooling has run to completion: all
five stratum baselines are shrunk onto a single number and the fitted model is
equivalent to one carrying no stratum term at all. Elk are detected several times
more often in harvest than in forest, so a stratum standard deviation of
effectively zero is not a finding about the strata, it is an estimation failure,
and it is silent.

**AIC prefers the fixed specification.** The median difference in AIC favours
the fixed effect in `r n_fixed_favoured` of `r n_periods_total` species-period
combinations, usually at all 16 spatial extents (Table S8.10). The fixed
specification carries three more estimated parameters than the random one (four
contrasts against one variance), so it wins these comparisons after being
charged a six-unit penalty for them.

**The collinearity cost that would argue for partial pooling does not
materialise.** All `r n_converged` of `r n_fits` fits converged under both
specifications. No variance inflation factor for a habitat predictor exceeds
`r round(vif_max_fixed, 2)` under the fixed specification against
`r round(vif_max_random, 2)` under the random one, both below the
conventional threshold of 5 (Table S8.6). Median standard errors are within 5%
of parity for `r n_se_parity` of `r n_se_total` species-predictor combinations,
and `r n_se_better` are estimated more precisely under the fixed specification
(Table S8.8).

**The reported inference is largely preserved, and where it moves it moves at
fine extents.** Of the `r n_profiles` species-period-predictor profiles,
`r n_peak_match` have an identical peak scale of effect and `r n_domain_match`
have identical domain structure under the two specifications (Table S8.2).
Cell-level sign classification agrees in `r agreement$n_agree` of
`r agreement$n_cells` cells (`r round(agreement$pct_agree, 1)`%) and the point
estimates correlate at r = `r round(agreement$r_estimates, 3)` (Table S8.3).

The changes are concentrated where the confounding is. Stratum explains a large
share of the variance in proportion cutblock harvest and human use intensity at
the finest extents and almost none beyond 3 km (Table S8.5), so
under the random intercept a stratum difference left unabsorbed had a fine-scale
predictor available to attach itself to. That is the mechanism behind the
profiles that change, and it is why broad-scale inference is unaffected: at
7 km there is nothing left to leak.

One consequence follows for how the main results read. Under the fixed
specification the habitat predictor coefficients are within-stratum
associations. A fine-scale coefficient answers whether the surrounding landscape
predicts detection rate over and above the stratum the camera sits in, and that
conditioning weakens as extent increases and the predictor comes to describe the
surrounding landscape rather than the camera location itself.
